name: Falljökull glacier walk
why: Crampons on a glacier that falls in a broken icefall from the Öræfajökull caldera: blue crevasses and moulins, with Iceland's highest peak above.
book: On the ice only with a licensed glacier guide; the park itself says so. Tours (about 4 h, of which 1-1.5 h on the ice; crampons, harness and helmet included) meet at the Skaftafell base and drive 25 minutes to the Falljökull car park.
water: Toilets and water at Skaftafell before the tour; nothing at the glacier. Carry 1 litre.
dangers: Crevasses and moulins: walk only in the guide's steps, never on your own.
The moraine in front of the glacier is loose and the meltwater streams are cold and fast.
Rain and wind come down off Öræfajökull quickly: a waterproof shell and gloves even in summer.
turnaround: Without a guide stop at the viewpoint at the foot of the ice. On a tour, the guide decides.

points.name: Falljökull car park on the moraine
points.note: End of the gravel track below the glacier, with the park's warning board. The guides fit crampons here or at Skaftafell, then walk about 30 minutes over the old moraine.

points.name: Falljökull ice edge, below the icefall
points.note: The viewpoint at the foot of the ice, where the crampons go on. The guided part goes up the lower tongue towards the icefall from the Öræfajökull caldera; the route changes with the ice and is not mapped.
